items.actClause: AN ACT to establish a statewide synthetic cannabinoid surrender program within the department of health; and to amend the general business law, the tax law and the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to prohibiting the sale of synthetic cannabinoids
items.lawCode: Add §399-hh, Gen Bus L; amd §§480, 1605 & 1607, Tax L; amd §§105, 106 & 118, ABC L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5619

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to establish a statewide synthetic cannabinoid surrender
program within the department of health; and to amend the general
business law, the tax law and the alcoholic beverage control law, in
relation to prohibiting the sale of synthetic cannabinoids

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

The bill prohibits the sale of synthetic cannabinoids by any retailer
and provides punishment to those retailers who violate this
prohibition. The bill punishes retailers with civil fines for selling
synthetic cannabinoids and for the most egregious violators
jeopardizes their ability to sell cigarettes, alcohol, and lottery
tickets.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

§ 1 - Creates a cannabinoid surrender program.

§ 2 - Amends the general business law to prohibit the sale of
synthetic cannabinoids. Additionally this section provides a $2,000
fine for the first violation, a $5,000 fine for the second violation,
and a third violation will result in the retailer's inability to sell
cigarettes, alcohol, or lottery tickets.

§ 3 - Amends the tax law to prohibit the issuance of a license to sell
cigarettes to retailers who have violated the synthetic cannabinoids
ban three or more times within a five year period.

§ 4 - Amends the tax law to suspend a license to sell cigarettes for
retailers who have violated the synthetic cannabinoids ban three or
more times within a five year period.

§ 5 - Amends the tax law to prohibit the issuance of a license to sell
lottery tickets to retailers who have violated the synthetic
cannabinoids ban three or more times within a five year period.

§ 6 - Amends the tax law to suspend a license to sell lottery tickets
to retailers who have violated the synthetic cannabinoids ban three or
more times within a five year period.

§ 7 - Amends the alcoholic beverage control law to prohibit the
issuance of a license to sell alcohol for off-premise consumption to
retailers who have violated the synthetic cannabinoids ban three or
more times within a five year period.

§ 8 - Amends the alcoholic beverage control law to prohibit the
issuance of a license to sell alcohol for on-premise consumption to
retailers who have violated the synthetic cannabinoids ban three or
more times within a five year period.

§ 9 - Amends the alcoholic beverage control law to empower the State
Liquor Authority to revoke a license to sell alcohol for any retailer
who has violated the synthetic cannabinoids ban three or more times
within a five year period.

§ 10 - allows municipalities to enact their own local laws related to
license revocations for businesses that manufacture, distribute, or
sell synthetic cannabinoids.

§ 11 - Act will take effect one hundred eighty days after becoming
law.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Over the last year, the dangers caused by synthetic cannabinoids (also
known as K2 or spice) and other synthetic drugs have come to the
forefront as localities deal with an influx of synthetic drug related
hospitalizations and related crime. The NYPD reported that over 1,900
people were admitted to hospital emergency rooms in NYC between April
1 and June 30, 2015. These drugs are being sold at local stores,
providing easy access to potential consumers. Under federal law, the
sale of synthetic marijuana is prohibited if sold for human
consumption. However, sellers of synthetic cannabinoids have exploited
a loophole in federal law by labeling packages of synthetic
cannabinoids as not intended for human consumption, instead being sold
as a type of incense.

Moreover, federal law enforcement lacks the resources to prosecute
these low level drug offenses, requiring a legislative solution under
state law. In 2012, Governor Cuomo announced an executive order in
which the sanitary code was amended to prohibit the sale, distribution
or possession of synthetic cannabinoids. Therefore, in order to
curtail the sale of synthetic cannabinoids this bill gives local
authorities the ability to target retailers who sell synthetic
cannabinoids and punish them appropriately.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the 180th day after it shall have become
law.

JUSTIFICATION:

Over the last year, the dangers caused by synthetic cannabinoids (also

er, sellers of synthetic cannabinoids have exploited a loophole in

Moreover, federal law enforcement lacks the resources to prosecute these
low level drug offenses, requiring a legislative solution under state

possession of synthetic cannabinoids. Therefore, in order to curtail the

them appropriately. This bill was amended in 2018 to alter the defi-
nition of "synthetic cannabinoid" to exclude those products approved by
the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or the NYS Department of Health.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This bill was introduced in 2015, and Passed the Senate in 2016 and
2017. The bill has not moved from the Assembly Committee or origin.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the 180th day after it shall have become
Law.
